concepts.title: Andrew Manson: A Young Doctor's Evening of Doubt
concepts.definition: Andrew Manson, newly out of medical school and assisting Dr Page in a Welsh mining town, walks home from a disheartening evening with Christine, doubting love and medicine alike. The night's drudgery leaves him questioning his profession just before the Morgan delivery calls him to duty.
concepts.key_idea: A doctor at low ebb -- doubt must be overcome by duty before skill can save anyone.
concepts.textbook_ref: kesp104.txt opening sections (andrew manson newly out of medical school, assistant to dr edward page, welsh mining town, evening with christine, doubt)

solution_steps.explain: A tiring round and a heart-aching evening leave Andrew sour on love and his profession's drudgery.
Joe Morgan waits at the door -- his wife, after years of marriage, is in labour.
The long, hard delivery will test everything the young doctor has and is.

concepts.title: The Stillborn Child and the Decision to Fight
concepts.definition: The mother is safely delivered, but the child lies lifeless -- a boy, seemingly stillborn. Refusing to accept defeat, Andrew remembers a method from observation and begins alternating hot and cold baths and rhythmic manipulation; the mother, meanwhile, needs a quick injection to steady her heart.
concepts.key_idea: Between despair and method -- a doctor's stubborn memory of one trick stands between death and a first cry.
concepts.textbook_ref: kesp104.txt delivery sections (stillborn child, basins hot and cold water, resuscitation efforts, injection for mother, midwife's despair)

solution_steps.explain: Andrew dashes an emergency injection to steady the exhausted mother's heart before returning to the child.
Wrapping the limp boy, he alternates basins of hot and cold water and rubs and presses the little body rhythmically.
Half a lifetime of effort compressed into minutes, he persists against the room's despair.

concepts.title: The First Cry: Triumph of Life and of the Doctor
concepts.definition: At last the child's chest heaves, skin pinks, and a cry rings through the house -- the stillborn lives. Andrew, drenched and trembling, realises what he has done; the evening's doubt about medicine is answered by a single act of saving, and he leaves knowing that a doctor's purpose is this.
concepts.key_idea: One cry answers every doubt -- medicine's meaning restored in a gasp of returned life.
concepts.textbook_ref: kesp104.txt closing sections (the child's cry, skin colour change, relief and triumph, andrew's realisation about his profession)

solution_steps.explain: The little chest lifts, colour floods back, and life announces itself in a cry.
Exhaustion gives way to exaltation; the doctor who doubted his craft has just embodied its highest purpose.
Birth names both the child's entry into life and the doctor's own rebirth into certainty.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Why did Andrew attend to the mother before continuing with the apparently stillborn child? Was this right?

solution_template.explain: The mother's heart was faltering; without the injection she could die while he worked on the child.
He calculated that minutes spent steadying her would not yet doom the baby.
Both lives were saved -- presence of mind under pressure is the chapter's portrait of medical judgment.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Trace the arc of Andrew Manson's feelings from the beginning to the end of the chapter.

solution_template.explain: He begins weary and disillusioned -- sour on love, seeing his profession as drudgery.
The delivery forces total commitment -- method, memory and will against death.
The child's cry restores meaning; doubt has been answered by deed, and the doctor is reborn with his patient.
